title: Workflow Mapping for AI: Finding the Right Automation Targets
author: Jason D.
excerpt: Not every workflow should be automated. Here's how to map your operations and identify where AI agents will deliver the highest ROI.
content:
The biggest mistake in AI automation isn't picking the wrong technology. It's picking the wrong workflow. Teams rush to automate what's visible ("we get so many support tickets!") instead of what's valuable ("this approval bottleneck costs us $50K/month in delays").

The Workflow Mapping Process

Before any AI work begins, map your operations end-to-end:

Step 1: Document the Current State

Walk through every step of the workflow with the people who do it daily. Not the managers — the operators. They know where the friction is.

Step 2: Identify Decision Points

Every workflow has decision points: route this ticket, approve this request, flag this anomaly. These are your automation candidates.

Step 3: Score Each Candidate

# automation_scoring.yaml
candidates:
  - name: "Ticket Routing"
    volume: HIGH          # How often does this happen?
    complexity: LOW       # How many rules/exceptions?
    data_quality: HIGH    # Is input data structured?
    business_value: HIGH  # What's the cost of doing it manually?
    score: 9/10

  - name: "Contract Review"
    volume: MEDIUM
    complexity: HIGH
    data_quality: LOW
    business_value: HIGH
    score: 5/10           # High value but hard to automate

Step 4: Prioritize by ROI

High volume + low complexity + good data quality = highest ROI. Start there. The complex, high-value workflows can come later once you have momentum and trust.

Common Mapping Mistakes

  • Mapping the ideal workflow — Map what actually happens, not what the process document says
  • Ignoring exceptions — The edge cases are where agents struggle most
  • Skipping the human context — Why do people make the decisions they make? What information do they use?
  • Over-scoping — You don't need to automate the entire workflow. Start with one decision point.

The best automation targets are boring. They're the repetitive, high-volume decisions that follow clear rules and have structured data. Save the ambitious stuff for later.

The Bottom Line

Workflow mapping is the unglamorous foundation that makes everything else possible. Skip it, and you'll automate the wrong thing. Do it well, and you'll know exactly where to invest for maximum impact.
